title: Normal and abnormal puerperium: involution, lochia, puerperal sepsis, mastitis and psychiatric disorders
subject: ss-obg
refs: Williams Obstetrics 25e Ch 36 (The Puerperium), Ch 37 (Puerperal Complications)
WHO Recommendations on Postnatal Care of the Mother and Newborn (2022)
RCOG Green-top Guideline No. 64b: Bacterial Sepsis following Pregnancy

steps.say: The puerperium spans the six-week postpartum interval during which maternal reproductive organs return to their pre-pregnant physiological state. The uterine fundus descends rapidly at approximately one to two centimeters daily, becoming an impalpable true pelvic organ by the tenth to twelfth postpartum day.
steps.tx: The physiological **puerperium** encompasses the 6-week postpartum recovery period. **Uterine involution** proceeds at a predictable rate of 1 to 2 cm per day, such that the uterine fundus, initially at the umbilicus, descends below the pubic symphysis to become an intrapelvic organ by day 10 to 12.

steps.say: Postpartum uterine discharge exhibits characteristic morphological stages reflecting decidual shedding and healing. Lochia rubra consists predominantly of fresh red blood and decidua during the initial three to four days, followed by serosa until day ten, and persistent lochia alba for up to six weeks.
steps.tx: Normal postpartum vaginal discharge, termed **lochia**, progresses through 3 stages: **lochia rubra** (erythrocytes and decidual debris for days 1 to 4), **lochia serosa** (serosanguinous fluid and leukocytes from days 5 to 10), and **lochia alba** (yellowish-white discharge rich in epithelial cells and mucus lasting 2 to 6 weeks).

rows: Heavy red bleeding; excess suggests subinvolution
Pink-brownish discharge; foul odor indicates endometritis
Mandates pelvic ultrasound and antibiotic therapy

steps.say: Septic pelvic thrombophlebitis involves suppurative bacterial thrombosis within the ovarian veins or deep pelvic venous plexuses. Patients present with persistent spiking fevers that fail to defervesce despite broad-spectrum antibiotics, resolving promptly upon initiating therapeutic low-molecular-weight heparin.
steps.tx: **Septic pelvic thrombophlebitis** (SPT) involves infected suppurative thrombosis within the **ovarian veins** or deep pelvic venous plexus. Patients manifest persistent spiking **fever refractory to antibiotics** alone, with diagnostic CT/MRI showing a thrombosed ovarian vein and fever resolving rapidly with **low-molecular-weight heparin**.

left.title: Septic Pelvic Thrombophlebitis
points: Bacterial endothelial injury and thrombosis of ovarian veins
Persistent high spiking fever despite 48-72h of broad-spectrum IV antibiotics
Contrast-enhanced pelvic CT confirms intraluminal filling defect

right.title: Therapeutic Heparin Challenge
points: Clinical defervescence typically occurs within 48 to 72 hours
Continue therapeutic anticoagulation for at least 6 weeks postpartum

steps.say: Puerperal pyrexia serves as an early clinical warning sign of serious postpartum infection. A oral temperature of 38.0 degrees Celsius or higher occurring on any two of the first ten postpartum days, excluding the initial 24 hours, mandates urgent microbiological and pelvic evaluation.
steps.tx: **Puerperal pyrexia** is defined as an oral temperature of 38.0 degrees C (100.4 degrees F) or higher occurring on any 2 of the first 10 days postpartum, excluding the initial 24 hours. The most frequent cause is **puerperal endometritis**, with cesarean delivery being the single most potent predisposing factor.

nodes.label: Document temperature >= 38.0 C on 2 occasions in first 10 days postpartum
Perform systematic septic workup (uterine tenderness, wound, breasts, urine, chest)
Identify postpartum endometritis (soft, tender uterus with foul lochia)
Initiate gold standard IV clindamycin and gentamicin therapy

steps.say: Puerperal endometritis represents a polymicrobial infection ascending from the lower genital tract after membrane rupture. The gold standard empirical antimicrobial regimen combines intravenous clindamycin at 900 milligrams every eight hours with intravenous gentamicin, providing over 90 to 95 percent clinical cure rates.
steps.tx: Postpartum **puerperal endometritis** is a polymicrobial ascending infection involving aerobes and anaerobes. The established gold standard regimen is intravenous **clindamycin** (900 mg every 8 hours) plus intravenous **gentamicin** (5 mg/kg daily), continuing until the patient remains afebrile for 24 to 48 hours.

rows: 2 g IV every 6 hours (added if resistant)

steps.say: Lactational mastitis results from milk stasis complicated by retrograde bacterial colonisation through fissured nipples. Staphylococcus aureus represents the predominant pathogen, producing intense focal breast erythema, localized induration, severe breast pain, and high spiking fevers.
steps.tx: **Lactational mastitis** typically develops 2 to 3 weeks postpartum, caused by ductal milk stasis and retrograde infection by **Staphylococcus aureus**. Patients present with a tender, wedged-shaped erythematous area of **focal breast pain**, systemic chills, and high fever requiring prompt antistaphylococcal therapy.

left.title: Infectious Mastitis Management
points: Oral dicloxacillin or cephalexin (500 mg QID for 10-14 days)
Essential: CONTINUE active breastfeeding or breast pumping
Avoids milk stasis and prevents abscess transformation

right.title: Breast Abscess Management
points: Develops when mastitis is neglected or inadequately treated
Presents with fluctuant, indurated, exquisitely tender mass
Ultrasound-guided needle aspiration or formal surgical drainage

steps.say: Distinguishing transient postpartum emotional lability from severe psychiatric illness is vital for maternal and infant safety. Postpartum blues affects up to 80 percent of mothers self-resolving by two weeks, while postpartum depression persists beyond two weeks, requiring structured psychotherapeutic and pharmacological intervention.
steps.tx: **Postpartum blues** represents a transient, benign mood disturbance affecting up to 70 to 80 percent of new mothers, resolving spontaneously within 10 to 14 days. Conversely, **postpartum depression** represents an unremitting depressive illness lasting beyond 2 weeks, characterized by vegetative symptoms and maternal detachment.

nodes.label: Screen postpartum mothers using Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS)
EPDS score < 10: reassure, normal emotional adaptation or mild blues
EPDS score >= 10 to 12: diagnose postpartum depression, start CBT and SSRIs (sertraline)
Delusions, hallucinations, or infanticidal thoughts: emergency postpartum psychosis

steps.say: Postpartum psychosis represents an acute, catastrophic psychiatric emergency occurring in one to two per thousand deliveries. Mothers present within two to four weeks with severe delirium, cognitive confusion, paranoid delusions, and hallucinations, carrying an alarming 4 percent risk of infanticide.
steps.tx: **Postpartum psychosis** is a medical emergency presenting with acute confusion, affective lability, auditory hallucinations, and bizarre **paranoid delusions** regarding the infant. Carrying an alarming 4 to 5 percent risk of **infanticide** and maternal suicide, it necessitates immediate hospitalization, separation precautions, and antipsychotic therapy.
